items.text: The CL-SciSumm Shared Task is the ﬁrst medium-scale shared task on scientiﬁc document summarization in the computational linguistics (CL) domain.
items.why: Defines what the CL-SciSumm Shared Task is.
items.plain: The CL-SciSumm Shared Task is the first medium-scale shared task on scientific paper summarization in computational linguistics.

items.text: In 2019, it comprised three tasks: (1A) identifying relationships between citing documents and the referred document, (1B) classifying the discourse facets, and (2) generating the abstractive summary.
items.why: Defines the three subtasks included in the 2019 shared task.
items.plain: In 2019, the task included three parts: matching citing sentences to the original text, classifying discourse categories, and generating an abstractive summary.

items.text: Task 1A: For each citance, identify the spans of text (cited text spans) in the RP that most accurately reﬂect the citance.
items.plain: Task 1A requires identifying the exact original text spans in the reference paper that a citation sentence refers to.

items.text: Task 1B: For each cited text span, identify what facet of the paper it belongs to, from a predeﬁned set of facets.
items.plain: Task 1B requires identifying which predefined research facet each cited text span belongs to.

items.text: For Task 1A, the best performance was shown by System 3 (Team UoM) [24].
items.why: States the winning system for Task 1A.
items.plain: System 3 (Team UoM) achieved the best performance in Task 1A.

items.text: The third best system was system 2 (Team CIST-BUPT) which was also the best performer for Task 1B, the classiﬁcation task.
items.why: States the winning system for Task 1B.
items.plain: System 2 (Team CIST-BUPT) came in third for Task 1A and performed best on Task 1B.

items.text: On the summarisation task, Task 2, System 3 (Team UoM) had the best performance against the abstract.
items.why: States the top system for Task 2 when compared to abstracts.
items.plain: System 3 performed best in Task 2 when evaluated against abstract summaries.

items.text: System 2 (Team CIST-BUPT) had the best performance for community and human summaries.
items.why: States the top system for Task 2 against community and human summaries.
items.plain: System 2 performed best in Task 2 when evaluated against community and human summaries.

items.text: The best Task 1a performance (sentence overlap F1) this year is 0.126 from System 3 [24] which is a deep learning system trained on augmented data.
items.why: Gives the headline score for Task 1A.
items.plain: The highest score on Task 1A sentence overlap F1 was 0.126 by System 3.

items.text: The best on CL-SciSumm ’19 Task 2 performance on human written summaries on ROUGE-2 is 0.278 by [10].
items.why: Gives the headline score for Task 2.
items.plain: The top score on Task 2 against human-written summaries was a ROUGE-2 score of 0.278 by System 2.

items.text: With a score of 0.514 System 3 also improves the state-of-the-art agasint abstracts by 0.2 on ROUGE-2 score.
items.why: Gives the top score for Task 2 against paper abstracts.
items.plain: System 3 set a new state-of-the-art score of 0.514 ROUGE-2 when compared against paper abstracts.

items.text: Traditional methods do better on Task 1a on small but clean training data.
items.why: Summarizes when traditional methods outperform deep learning.
items.plain: Traditional methods perform better on Task 1A when using small, clean training datasets.

items.text: Deep learning methods take over on large bu tnoisy data.
items.why: Summarizes when deep learning outperforms traditional methods.
items.plain: Deep learning models outperform traditional methods when trained on large, noisy datasets.

items.text: We found that data augmentation for Task 1a may have helped deep learning models but not traditional machine learning methods.
items.why: States key finding on data augmentation across model types.
items.plain: Adding more training data for Task 1A helped deep learning models, but did not help traditional machine learning methods.

items.text: It also appears that deep learning methods perform better than traditional methods across the board when they have enough training data.
items.why: States the main takeaways about deep learning across all tasks.
items.plain: Deep learning approaches outperform traditional approaches across all tasks when given sufficient training data.
